title: Data-centric machine learning prioritizes compounds for Trypanosoma cruzi assays
summary: Ensemble supervised classifiers trained on curated phenotypic activity data prioritized eight repurposing compounds for clinically relevant parasite-stage assays. The article reports six selected compounds with predicted trypanocidal effects, while identifying cytotoxicity as a caveat for two amastigote candidates; mifepristone showed trypomastigote activity. These are in-vitro strain-specific outcomes, not clinical efficacy or novel molecular entities.

evidence.tested: Primary article reports eight in-silico hits and selected-stage experimental confirmation; tables qualify cytotoxicity caveats.
evidence.unknown: Prior compound activity and some full model/supplement details remain for later audit; selected repurposed compounds are not novel molecules.
evidence.ai_role: Data-centric supervised ensembles prioritize repurposing candidates for distinct parasite-stage assays.
